written.myAnswer: The line of action of a force is the straight line along which the force acts.

The moment (torque) of a force is the turning effect of the force; its magnitude is the force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation to the force’s line of action. If r is the distance from the axis to the point of application and θ is the angle between r and F, the perpendicular moment arm is r sinθ. Therefore, τ = F(r sinθ) = rF sinθ.
